Prevention: Contact the local agriculture office for an up-to-date list of available varieties.
Synchronize rice planting with other farms
Transplant older seedlings (>3 weeks) to reduce viral disease susceptibility transmitted by leafhoppers.
Apply sufficient nitrogen to avoid contributing to population outbreaks by applying too much nitrogen, or hindering plant recovery from green leaf hopper (GLH) damage by not applying enough nitrogen.
Encourage biological control agents: small wasps (parasitize the eggs), mirid bug; Strepsipterans, fungal pathogens (attacks both nymph and adult).
Monitoring: When populations appear to be increasing, check twice a week, spray chemicals if outbreak (>5
Direct Control: GLH attack in young rice seedlings, where the plants are still small/ short (below 20cm), use net scarf to catch/ collect and kill.
Restrictions: Spray onto top of rice canopy as
GLH tend to feed at the top.
